extra.message: User-controlled parameter params["id"] is concatenated directly into the SQL SELECT statement passed to cursor.execute(). This allows boolean/time-based and UNION-based SQL injection (e.g. ?id=2 UNION ALL SELECT ... or ?id=2 AND SUBSTR(...)).
User-controlled parameter params["comment"] is formatted directly into an INSERT statement via string interpolation and passed to cursor.execute(). This allows SQL injection.

The login query concatenates params.get("password") directly into the SQL string passed to cursor.execute() without sanitization. This permits authentication bypass via SQL injection (e.g. password=' OR '1'='1).
pickle.loads() is called on user-supplied data from params["object"]. Unpickling attacker-controlled data allows arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payloads.
User-controlled params["domain"] is concatenated into a shell command 'nslookup ' + domain executed with subprocess.run(shell=True). This allows OS command injection (e.g. domain=;cat /etc/passwd).

exec() executes the contents of a file/URL referenced by user-controlled params["include"]. Combined with the remote-file fetch (urllib.request.urlopen) on line 56, an attacker can supply a remote URL containing arbitrary Python code, leading to remote code execution (RFI).
params["include"] is used to open a local file or fetch a remote URL via urllib.request.urlopen without validation, enabling remote/local file inclusion which is then passed to exec() on line 57.

cwe: CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require

extra.message: params["path"] is passed to open(os.path.abspath(params["path"])) without sanitization, allowing arbitrary local file read via path traversal (e.g. path=/etc/passwd or ../../).

When params["path"] contains '://', it is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(), allowing the server to make requests to attacker-specified URLs (SSRF), e.g. fetching internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.

lxml.etree.parse() parses user-supplied XML (params["xml"]) with an XMLParser configured load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks for local file disclosure and SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled params["name"] is interpolated directly into an XPath expression .//user[name/text()='%s'] passed to xpath(). This allows XPath injection to extract arbitrary nodes (e.g. password fields).
params["v"] is reflected unescaped into the HTML response via re.sub substitution, allowing reflected Cross-Site Scripting.
The username from params is reflected unescaped into the HTML 'Welcome %s' response, allowing reflected XSS. (The regex strips non-word chars but the value is still echoed into HTML.)
The /users.json endpoint reflects user-controlled params["callback"] directly into the response body as a JSONP wrapper without validation, allowing reflected XSS / JSONP-based script injection.
params["redir"] is injected into a <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=..."> tag without validation, allowing open redirect to attacker-controlled URLs and potential HTML/header injection.

params["size"] is converted to int and used to build a string of '#'*size repeated 'size' times, producing O(size^2) memory/CPU consumption. A large size value causes denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption.
The Content-Type response header is built using user-controlled params.get("charset") without validation, allowing HTTP response header injection / manipulation of the charset value.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers (HTTP Response Splitting)

extra.message: On any exception, the full Python traceback (traceback.format_exc()) or command output is returned to the client in the HTTP response body, exposing sensitive internal information such as file paths, source code, and system details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The response explicitly sets the X-XSS-Protection header to 0, disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter and increasing the impact of reflected XSS vulnerabilities in this application.

The SESSIONID session cookie is set without HttpOnly or Secure flags (via a meta http-equiv Set-Cookie), exposing the session identifier to client-side scripts and transmission over insecure channels.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag

extra.message: Hardcoded user credentials (usernames and plaintext passwords such as admin / 7en8aiDoh!) are embedded in the USERS_XML constant and loaded into the application database.
